OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 18, 2026 (11:20 a.m. EST)

STATUS: ACTUAL DIVERSION CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Santee Cooper's official operational feed is dated November 18 and its latest daily lake elevations are dated November 17 (one-day reporting lag). Individual measurement timestamps, matching vertical gauge datums, and a direct canal flow observation have not been independently established. The operator's daily lake elevations should not be treated as simultaneous hydraulic-head measurements.

OPERATOR DAILY ELEVATIONS (feet; gauge comparability not independently confirmed): November 17 Lake Marion 74.13 and Lake Moultrie 74.06, nominal Marion-minus-Moultrie difference +0.07 ft. November 16 Lake Marion 74.16 and Lake Moultrie 74.09, nominal difference +0.07 ft. Both lakes fell 0.03 ft between reported dates, and the nominal difference was unchanged. November 18 lake elevations are not yet published in the operator daily table. This difference is arithmetic only; it is not independently verified instantaneous hydraulic head.

HYDRO OPERATIONS (Santee Cooper feed updated November 18; TENTATIVE, not actual generation observations): Jefferies November 18 8 a.m.–midnight and November 19 6 a.m.–10 p.m. St. Stephen not scheduled November 18 or 19. November 17 operator daily discharge entries: Jefferies 3,613; St. Stephen 0; units not independently reconciled here. These are facility entries, NOT measured Diversion Canal flow; schedules or generation do not prove canal current or direction.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL INFERENCE ONLY: If lake elevations are referenced to a common vertical datum and comparable times, Marion's nominally higher reported elevation would be consistent with potential Marion-to-Moultrie movement. The small +0.07 ft nominal difference, unchanged from November 16, cannot verify the direction or strength of actual current. Wind setup, operations, and localized water levels may alter conditions. No defensible qualitative current-strength rating is available. Actual canal direction, velocity and discharge remain NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED.

wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
temperature_analysis: WATER TEMPERATURE REPORT — November 19, 2026 (8:06 a.m. EST). CURRENT PRIMARY USGS TEMPERATURE DATA NOT VERIFIED. Attempted the USGS instantaneous-values endpoint for parameter 00010 (water temperature, degrees Celsius) at sites 02171000 and 02172002; retrieval was unsuccessful. No November 19 primary readings, exact observation timestamps, freshness measurements, or matching 24-hour historical values could be established. Therefore no current temperatures or 24-hour changes are reported. Last documented ATSC dashboard screenshot showed November 16 at 7:45 a.m. EST: Pineville bottom water 61.3°F and Moncks Corner downstream tailrace 62.8°F. These are older, not independently primary-verified values, and are NOT today's temperatures. Pineville measures bottom water at Lake Marion, while Moncks Corner measures downstream tailrace canal water below Lake Moultrie; neither is a lake-wide surface-water measurement, nor should their difference be interpreted as a lake-to-lake temperature comparison. Seasonal cooling can influence forage and blue catfish distribution, but no present fish location or feeding activity is established by these readings. Check latest source timestamps at https://atsclakes.com/#conditions and primary USGS station pages https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02171000/ and https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172002/ .
